Holonomic functions

Source: vignettes/holonomic.Rmd
holonomic.Rmd
library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); n <- Symbol("n")

This vignette covers sympy.holonomic: holonomic functions, the differential and recurrence operators that define them, and conversions to and from hypergeometric and Meijer G functions.

Holonomic functions and operators

A holonomic function is a solution of a linear ordinary differential equation with polynomial coefficients, together with initial conditions. Sums and products of holonomic functions are holonomic, so many manipulations reduce to operations on differential operators.

DifferentialOperators() creates the algebra of operators in D_x. Below, p is e^x (the solution of y' = y, y(0) = 1) and q is \sin x (the solution of y'' = -y, y(0) = 0, y'(0) = 1).

R <- DifferentialOperators(holonomic_ring(x), "Dx")
Dx <- R$Dx
p <- HolonomicFunction(Dx - 1, x, 0, list(1))
q <- HolonomicFunction(Dx^2 + 1, x, 0, list(0, 1))
to_expr_holonomic(p)
#> exp(x)
to_expr_holonomic(q * q)
#> sin(x)^2

expr_to_holonomic() converts an expression, after which series, sequences of coefficients, derivatives, and numerical values are available.

h <- expr_to_holonomic(exp(x) * sin(x), x)
series_holonomic(h, n = 6)
#> x + x^2 + x^3/3 - x^5/30 + O(x^6)
to_expr_holonomic(diff_holonomic(expr_to_holonomic(sin(x), x)))
#> cos(x)
to_expr_holonomic(expr_to_holonomic(log(1 + x), x))
#> log(x + 1)
to_hyper(expr_to_holonomic(exp(x), x))
#> hyper((), (), x)

evalf_holonomic() integrates the differential equation numerically along a path of points, with the fourth order Runge-Kutta method by default, and returns the values at those points. Integrating y' = y from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.1 approximates e \approx 2.718282:

path <- as.list(seq(0.1, 1, by = 0.1))
vals <- evalf_holonomic(p, path)
vapply(vals, sstr, "")
#>  [1] "1.10517083333333" "1.22140257085069" "1.34985849706254" "1.49182424008069"
#>  [5] "1.64872063859684" "1.82211796209193" "2.01375162659678" "2.22553956329232"
#>  [9] "2.45960141378007" "2.71827974413517"
sstr(evalf_holonomic(expr_to_holonomic(sin(x), x), path)[[10]])
#> [1] "0.841470477800274"

The last value approximates \sin(1) \approx 0.841471.

Transformations

change_x() substitutes a polynomial for the variable, shift_x() shifts it, and change_ics() moves the point where the initial conditions are given. holonomic_degree() is the largest degree of a polynomial coefficient of the annihilator, and holonomic_indicial() the indicial equation at the origin.

shift_x(p, 2)
#> HolonomicFunction((-1) + (1)*Dx, x, -2, [1])
change_ics(expr_to_holonomic(sin(x), x), 1)
#> HolonomicFunction((1) + (1)*Dx^2, x, 1, [sin(1), cos(1)])
change_x(p, 2 * x)
#> HolonomicFunction((-1) + (1)*Dx, 2*x, 0, [1])
holonomic_degree(expr_to_holonomic(exp(x^2), x))
#> [1] 1
holonomic_indicial(expr_to_holonomic(sqrt(x) * exp(x), x))
#> [[1]]
#> 1/2
#> 
#> attr(,"multiplicity")
#> [1] 1

composition() substitutes an algebraic expression into a holonomic function. Without initial conditions only the annihilator is computed; with them, the result can be converted back to an expression.

composition(HolonomicFunction(Dx - 1, x), x^2 + x)
#> HolonomicFunction((-2*x - 1) + (1)*Dx, x)
to_expr_holonomic(composition(p, x^2, 0, list(1)))
#> exp(x^2)

integrate_holonomic() integrates, either as a new holonomic function or over limits:

integrate_holonomic(q, list(x, 0, 1))
#> 1 - cos(1)
to_expr_holonomic(integrate_holonomic(p, list(x, 0, x)))
#> exp(x) - 1

Recurrences

The coefficients of the power series of a holonomic function satisfy a linear recurrence. RecurrenceOperators() builds the algebra of shift operators, HolonomicSequence() a sequence defined by a recurrence, and to_sequence() the recurrence for a holonomic function.

RS <- RecurrenceOperators(holonomic_ring(n), "Sn")
Sn <- RS$Sn
HolonomicSequence(Sn - n - 1, list(1))
#> HolonomicSequence((-n - 1) + (1)Sn, n), u(0) = 1
to_sequence(expr_to_holonomic(x^3, x))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> HolonomicSequence((n), n), u(0) = 1 
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> 3
#> 
#> [[1]][[3]]
#> [1] 1
to_sequence(p)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> HolonomicSequence((-1) + (n + 1)Sn, n), u(0) = 1 
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] 0

Hypergeometric and Meijer G functions

from_hyper() and from_meijerg() turn special functions into holonomic functions, and to_meijerg() goes back.

from_hyper(hyper(list(1, 1), list(Rational(3, 2)), x^2 / 4))
#> HolonomicFunction((4*x) + (5*x^2 - 8)*Dx + (x^3 - 4*x)*Dx^2, x, 1, [2*sqrt(3)*pi/9, -4*sqrt(3)*pi/27 + 4/3])
from_meijerg(meijerg(list(), list(), list(0), list(), x))
#> HolonomicFunction((1) + (1)*Dx, x, 0, [1])
to_meijerg(expr_to_holonomic(sin(x), x))
#> sqrt(pi)*x*meijerg(((), ()), ((0,), (-1/2,)), x^2/4)/2
